title: A quotient of a Noetherian complete local ring is a Noetherian complete local ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring which is complete, i.e. $\mathfrak m$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and let $I\subsetneq R$ be a proper ideal. Then $R/I$ is a Noetherian local ring, with maximal ideal $\bar{\mathfrak m}=\mathfrak m/I$, which is $\bar{\mathfrak m}$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0325 (lemma-quotient-complete-local, line 44811), first sentence ('Any quotient of R is also a Noetherian complete local ring'); proof via Lemma 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor)

proof.text: (Noetherian.) The quotient map $\pi:R\to R/I$ is a surjective ring homomorphism and $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], so $R/I$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian].

source.place: Lemma 0325 (lemma-quotient-complete-local), proof, first sentence: 'The ring S is Noetherian by Lemma 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence)'

proof.text: (Local, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/I$.) Since $I\ne R$ is a proper ideal of the local ring $R$, it is contained in a maximal ideal, which is $\mathfrak m$, the only one; so $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Hence $R/I$ is a nonzero local ring whose maximal ideal is the image $\bar{\mathfrak m}=\pi(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak m/I$ [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure].

source.place: Lemma 0325 (lemma-quotient-complete-local), statement ('Any quotient of R is also a ... local ring'); the step is written out by the agent

proof.text: (Completeness as an $R$-module.) The $R$-module $N=R/I$ is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], by the class $\bar1$ of $1$. As $R$ is Noetherian and $\mathfrak m$-adically complete, $N$ is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian] (applied with $J=\mathfrak m$): the canonical map $c:N\to\varprojlim_nN/\mathfrak m^nN$, $x\mapsto(x\bmod\mathfrak m^nN)_n$, is bijective.

source.place: Lemma 0325 (lemma-quotient-complete-local), proof, second sentence: 'As an R-module S is complete by Lemma 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor)'

proof.text: (From the module to the ring.) For $n\ge1$, $\mathfrak m^nN$ is the $R$-submodule of $R/I$ generated by the $a\bar x$ with $a\in\mathfrak m^n$, $\bar x\in R/I$, i.e. $\mathfrak m^nN=\pi(\mathfrak m^n)=(\mathfrak m^n+I)/I$; and $\pi(\mathfrak m^n)=\pi(\mathfrak m)^n=\bar{\mathfrak m}^n$, since $\mathfrak m^n$ is additively generated by products $a_1\cdots a_n$ ($a_i\in\mathfrak m$) with $\pi(a_1\cdots a_n)=\pi(a_1)\cdots\pi(a_n)$, and $\bar{\mathfrak m}^n$ is additively generated by such products of images. So $N/\mathfrak m^nN$ and $(R/I)/\bar{\mathfrak m}^n$ are the same quotient of the abelian group $R/I$, with the same transition maps (reduction), and the canonical map $c$ of step 3 is the canonical map $R/I\to\varprojlim_n(R/I)/\bar{\mathfrak m}^n$, $x\mapsto(x\bmod\bar{\mathfrak m}^n)_n$, of the $\bar{\mathfrak m}$-adic completion of the ring $R/I$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. It is bijective by step 3, so $R/I$ is $\bar{\mathfrak m}$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. With steps 1 and 2 this is the statement.
